question: What three types of signs are required at an interchange exit-ramp terminal where wrong-way entry could inadvertently occur?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The three types of signs shown for an exit-ramp terminal where wrong-way entry could occur are the DO NOT ENTER (R5-1) sign, the WRONG WAY (R5-1a) sign, and ONE WAY (R6-1/R6-2) signs. The text evidence supplied for this question (Specific Service signing, ramp control signals, and cloverleaf guide signing) does not contain the governing exit-ramp wrong-way provision (Section 2B.48), so the answer rests on the visual evidence, which includes the Section 2B.46 standard text and Figure 2B-15. Standards (mandatory): - From the visible Section 2B.46 text [Image 3]: "The DO NOT ENTER (R5-1) sign (see Figure 2B-13) shall be used at the following locations: … B. The intersection of an interchange exit ramp with a crossroad as specified in Section 2B.48 (see Figure 2B-15)." - Note: The six text-based Standard provisions provided (Sections 2J.06, 2J.07, 2J.08, 4P.02, 2G.15, 2E.33) do not address wrong-way signing at exit-ramp terminals and cannot support this answer. Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 2B-15 illustrates the exit-ramp termination layout with DO NOT ENTER signs facing potential wrong-way entrants, WRONG WAY signs along the exit ramp, and ONE WAY signs at the ramp/crossroad junction (with some installations marked optional). - [Image 2] The full page 112 view confirms Figure 2B-15, "Example of Application of Regulatory Signing and Pavement Markings at an Exit Ramp Termination to Deter Wrong-Way Entry," showing the combined DO NOT ENTER, WRONG WAY, and ONE WAY sign application. - [Image 3] Page 150 (MUTCD page 109) shows Section 2B.46 requiring the DO NOT ENTER sign at "the intersection of an interchange exit ramp with a crossroad as specified in Section 2B.48," and Figure 2B-13 depicting the R5-1 DO NOT ENTER, R5-1a WRONG WAY, and R6-1/R6-2 ONE WAY signs. - [Image 4] The table of contents lists Figure 2B-15 ("Example of Application of Regulatory Signing and Pavement Markings at an Exit Ramp Termination to Deter Wrong-Way Entry") and related figures 2B-13 and 2B-17, corroborating the sign family involved. - [Image 5] Figure 2D-18's note 3 directs readers to "Section 2B.48 and Figure 2B-15 for an example of regulatory signing and pavement markings at an exit ramp termination to deter wrong-way entry," confirming that Section 2B.48 governs this application. Citations: - Figure 2B-15 (p.112) - Page 153 - Page 150 - Page 29 - Page 297
gold_answer: At least one ONE WAY sign for each crossroad travel direction, at least one DO NOT ENTER sign near the downstream end of the exit ramp, and at least one WRONG WAY sign on the exit ramp facing wrong-way road users are required.
